$comment: Hand-maintained. There is no generator and no --write flag, and that is deliberate.
The dependency baseline is a ratchet you regenerate with one command, because those
findings are debt being paid down. This file is not that. A secret is either a false
positive or an incident, and a --write flag here would let a real leak be accepted
with one command. Every entry is added by hand and needs a reason a reviewer can check.
Entries key on path plus a SHA-256 prefix of the matched text, never the text itself,
so accepting a finding never writes the string back into the repository. The id is
printed by `npm run lint:secrets` next to each finding. Note that a hash only conceals
a high-entropy value, and a real credential should be rotated rather than recorded
here anyway. Moving an accepted string to a new file fails until that path is added,
which is the point: the set of hardcoded key literals cannot grow unreviewed.
The demo stack no longer ships a committed bootstrap key. `docker compose --profile
demo up --build` mints a random global-admin key at seed time, prints it once, and
hands it to the web container out of band, so there is nothing to allowlist for it.
See issue #169 and packages/demo/api/src/seed.ts. Migration 011 removed the same key
from the schema migrations earlier, for the same reason.
The entries below are truncated key examples in the docs site and one Storybook
fixture: elided stand-ins that illustrate the shape of a key_prefix, a plaintext_key
and a sensitive config value, plus two test constants that hold an env-var NAME rather
than a credential. They are too short to be minted keys and are not placeholder-shaped,
so the rule cannot tell them apart from a real short literal without a human saying so.
Note that this file names no key text anywhere, including in these comments. That is
the rule it exists to enforce, so writing an example here would fail the check, which
is how it should be.
